theater: 河東郡蒲州與安邑、白徑嶺

battle.name: 河東之戰
battle.theater: 河東郡蒲州與安邑、白徑嶺
battle.brief: 唐肅宗至德二載（757）二月，兵部尚書、朔方節度使郭子儀率師自洛交出發，策反河東（蒲州）內應，夜襲奪城，敗叛將崔乾祐於城北，追奔安邑、白徑嶺而克之。卡面那具秦弩正是此役的關鍵：城頭的弩機因內應而無從發射，野戰中弩手列陣封路，取代弓手成為壓制與追殺的骨幹。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰雙方是唐廷與安史叛軍所立的偽燕。唐方由兵部尚書、朔方節度使郭子儀統軍，兵分兩路：一路自洛交（今陝西富縣）直指河東郡治蒲州（今山西永濟西南蒲州鎮），一路分兵趨馮翊（今陝西大荔縣），掩護主攻方向；參戰者以朔方、河中兩鎮兵為骨幹，附有京畿宿衛與隨軍聽用的蕃部騎兵，回鶻盟軍則由僕固懷恩居中聯絡，作為盟軍另立一軍。燕方以崔乾祐為河東守將，轄城內守軍與城北營兵，其編制仍帶著河北成德、范陽、平盧等節度使部的底子，步騎混編，野戰以騎兵突擊、攻城靠雲梯撞車見長。安慶緒弒父自立之後，坐鎮洛陽、鄴城，嚴莊掌機要，燕政權的兵權其實分散在各節度使手中，調度極不統一。唐方是號令歸一的行軍總制，燕方則是各自為戰、互不接應的鬆散聯盟，這一點在河東城下直接決定了勝負。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Tang court and the rebel state of Yan created by the An Lushan rebellion. On the Tang side the army was commanded by Guo Ziyi, Minister of War and Military Governor of Shuofang, and moved in two columns: one marched straight from Luojiao (present-day Fuxian, Shaanxi) on the seat of Hedong Commandery at Puzhou (the town of Puzhou southwest of Yongji, Shanxi), while a detachment turned toward Fengyi (present-day Dali County, Shaanxi) to cover the direction of the main effort. The troops were drawn mainly from the garrisons of Shuofang and Hezhong, with capital guards and steppe cavalry serving along with the column, while the Uyghur allies, whose treaty was brokered by Pugu Huai'en, marched as a separate allied host. On the Yan side stood Cui Qianyou, who held Hedong as garrison commander, with the city garrison and the troops encamped north of the wall; his command still carried the character of the Hebei circuit armies of Chengde, Fanyang and Pinglu, infantry and cavalry mixed, strong in mounted surprise in the field and reliant on scaling towers and battering rams before a city. After An Qingxu killed his father and took the throne he sat at Luoyang and later Yecheng, with Yan Zhuang directing policy, while the real military authority remained dispersed among the circuit governors and could not be concentrated. The Tang field army was a single command under one man; the rebels were a loose coalition of separate commands unable to support one another, and that difference decided the outcome below the walls of Hedong.
people: 主導者是兵部尚書、朔方節度使郭子儀。他判斷河東正卡在洛陽與長安之間，先取河東便可威攝潼關、切斷兩京聯繫，於是趕在安慶緒弒父、叛軍內訧之際動手。他先派心腹郭懷文、郭俊潛入河東，聯絡仍效忠唐朝的官軍與官吏，約定內應；河東司戶韓旻翻牆出城，親自引導唐軍在十一日夜摸黑進抵城下，舉火為號，城內外同時發動。城破之後，郭子儀命自己的兒子郭旰與部將僕固懷恩出城迎戰，大敗崔乾祐於城北，再乘勝追擊。僕固懷恩同時是回鶻盟軍的穿線人，先前單騎入蕃部借兵的約議由他而起。燕方守將崔乾祐在夢中被驚醒，越城北逃，收攏城北叛軍反攻不成，率殘部東走安邑，於城門下企圖入城歇息，卻被預伏的鄉里截殺，隻身經白徑嶺南逃。唐肅宗則乘叛軍內訧下詔收復兩京，安慶緒弒父自立，成為此役得以展開的關鍵外部條件。
peopleEn: The man in command was Guo Ziyi, Minister of War and Military Governor of Shuofang. He judged that Hedong lay exactly between Luoyang and Chang'an, so that taking it would allow him to overawe Tong Pass and to cut the two capitals off from each other, and he moved at once, while the Yan regime was torn apart by the killing of An Lushan. He first sent trusted agents, Guo Huaiwen and Guo Jun, secretly into Hedong to make contact with Tang officers and civilians still loyal to the dynasty and to agree on a rising from within; Han Min, the registrar of Hedong, climbed over the city wall and came out to meet the army, and personally guided the Tang troops to the foot of the walls in the dark of the night of the eleventh, a torch being the signal, so that the attack began inside and outside at the same moment. Once the city had fallen, Guo Ziyi sent his own son Guo Gan and his general Pugu Huai'en out of the city to meet the counter-attack, crushing Cui Qianyou north of the wall and then pressing the pursuit. Pugu Huai'en was at the same time the intermediary with the Uyghur allies, the compact for borrowing their riders having been set on foot by his own hand. On the Yan side, Cui Qianyou was roused from his sleep, escaped over the wall to the north, gathered the rebel troops there and failed to turn them back, then led the remnants east to Anyi; at the gate of that city he tried to force his way in to rest, only to be cut down by townsmen who had been posted in ambush, and he escaped alone over the White Path Ridge to the south. On the Tang side the emperor Xuanzong took advantage of the succession crisis in the rebel camp to issue the order to recover the two capitals, and the fact that An Qingxu had killed his father was the key external condition that made this battle possible.
kits: 卡面是秦弩，這種弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓，守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。河東之戰正好把這條守則的兩面都演了出來：燕軍崔乾祐據州城固守，城頭本可列弩封鎖城根，唐軍卻不走正面強攻，而是在夜裡以內應開路、翻牆殺出，令城頭的弩始終無從發射，攻城器械與遠射優勢都沒能派上用場；城破之後的野戰中，弩的價值轉到進攻方一邊，弩手成列以定距射擊封鎖道路、壓制潰兵，逼近與追殺的骨幹落在弩陣與騎兵的配合上。戰場上的其他裝備同樣有跡可循：叛軍隨帶雲梯、撞車等攻城器械，唐軍夜襲則靠火把、繩梯與破門器具；輕裝騎兵是崔乾祐連夜奔逃與郭子儀乘勝追擊的兩端速度；步行士卒以盾、橫刀、陌刀結陣，應對城北反攻。安邑城下的僵局還透出另一個裝備問題：叛軍「又飢又累」，說明其糧食、鞋履與體力早已耗盡；而唐軍取下河東、取得河中倉廩之後，弩箭、糧秣與甲兵才有穩定來源。
kitsEn: The card shows a Chinese crossbow, a weapon whose trigger mechanism stores the pull of the string, so that it shoots far faster than a bow; the side holding the walls relies on it to keep the assaulting men pinned outside. The battle of Hedong acted out both faces of that rule. Cui Qianyou of the Yan garrison held the prefectural city on the defensive, and the wall-top could have been lined with crossbows to seal the foot of the walls; the Tang army instead refused a frontal assault and came at night, led in by the men inside who opened the way, so that the wall crossbows never got the chance to loose and neither the besiegers' scaling gear nor their advantage in distance shooting was of any use. Once the city was taken, the value of the crossbow shifted to the attacking side: rows of crossbowmen fired at fixed ranges to seal the road and press the fleeing rebels, and the business of closing in and killing came to rest on the cooperation of the crossbow line with the horse. Other equipment on the field is equally traceable. The rebels brought scaling towers and battering rams with them; the Tang night attack worked by torchlight, rope ladders and the tools needed to break the gate. Light horse gave the speed at both ends of the day, in Cui Qianyou's flight by night and in Guo Ziyi's pursuit; foot soldiers closed up with shields, sabres and glaives to meet the counter-attack north of the city. The deadlock at Anyi also exposed a second problem of equipment: the rebels were 'both hungry and exhausted', showing that their food, footwear and stamina had long since run out, whereas after the Tang took Hedong and gained the granaries of Hezhong, crossbow bolts, grain and armour had a steady source at last.
tactics: 郭子儀此役的戰術核心是里應外合配合夜襲。兵分兩路：主力自洛交出發，循洛水、渭水北上，再沿黃河東岸直趨蒲州；偏師攻取馮翊，既是取險以分敵，也是使燕軍首尾不能相顧。突擊定在十一日夜，唐軍由韓旻等引導，偃旗息鼓摸黑進抵城下，以火為號，內應郭俊等自內殺出，外兵同時由城根爬城而入，破解了燕軍的城防。在此之前，他先做的並非攻擊而是策反——派郭懷文、郭俊潛行入城，在守軍內部找可以開門的人，這一步決定了後續的成敗。城既已下，郭子儀沒有停在城內整頓，而是趁亂追擊：崔乾祐在城北集結反攻，郭子儀遣郭旰、僕固懷恩出城迎戰，以弩陣定住陣腳，以騎兵縱橫，打崩了反攻部隊；繼而以步騎並行追擊，斷其歸路，收殲與俘獲都發生在城外野地，而非城牆之下。安邑城下的結局則顯示追擊可以做到什麼：叛軍飢疲爭門而入，門閘落下，預伏的鄉里自內截殺，崔乾祐最後取道白徑嶺向河南方向逃走才算脫出。整體而言，此役自興師到克城不過數日，靠的是策反、夜襲與乘勝追擊三者銜接，而不是正面硬攻。
tacticsEn: The core of Guo Ziyi's method in this campaign was a rising from within combined with a night assault. The army was divided: the main body left Luojiao, followed the Luo and Wei rivers northward and then ran along the eastern bank of the Yellow River to Puzhou; the flank column attacked Fengyi, both to seize a covered angle and to divide the enemy so that the Yan forces could not watch each other's front and rear. The blow was set for the night of the eleventh. Guided by Han Min and the others, the Tang troops moved on darkened banners and muffled drums until they stood beneath the walls, a torch was given as the signal, the insiders led by Guo Jun struck out from within while the outside troops climbed the wall from the foot at the same time, and the Yan defence was broken open. Before that, what Guo Ziyi had done was not to attack but to subvert: he sent Guo Huaiwen and Guo Jun secretly into the city to find men inside the garrison who would open the gate, and that single step decided the outcome of everything that followed. With the city taken, Guo Ziyi did not stay inside to reform his troops but pressed the pursuit while the enemy was still disordered. Cui Qianyou collected his men north of the city and counter-attacked; Guo Ziyi sent Guo Gan and Pugu Huai'en out of the city to meet them, the crossbow line fixing the front and the horse sweeping the flank, and the counter-attack came apart. He followed with foot and horse together, cutting the road of retreat, and the killing and the taking of prisoners were done in the open ground outside the walls rather than at the foot of them. The end at Anyi shows how far a pursuit can be pressed: the hungry, exhausted rebels forced their way through the gate, the gate was dropped behind them, and the townsmen posted in ambush struck them from within; only by taking the road over the White Path Ridge towards Henan did Cui Qianyou get clear. In sum, the whole campaign took no more than a few days from the march to the capture of the city, and it was won by the linking of three steps, the subversion, the night assault and the relentless pursuit, not by any frontal effort.
data: 可核的數字集中在《資治通鑑》第二百一十九卷唐紀三十五。時間是唐肅宗至德二載（757）二月，事前正月安慶緒在洛陽弒其父安祿山自立；突擊定在十一日夜。兵員方面，資治通鑑記唐軍「殲滅守城叛軍近千人」，又記追擊中「殲敵四千人，俘虜五千人」，安邑城下入城叛軍被全殲而人數未載；回鶻方面另記僕固懷恩前一年單騎借得回鶻兵七千五百騎，此役隨軍但未見參與河東攻城。距離上，洛交（今陝西富縣）至河東蒲州直線約二百八十里、逾一百四十公里，實際行軍需循洛水、渭水、黃河通道折轉，數日而至；河東蒲州至安邑（今山西運城東北）約六十里，崔乾祐由安邑再往南經白徑嶺（今山西平陸西北）入河南，是一日之內的連續奔竄。戰果另有一層意義：同年十月唐軍收復長安，十二月進取洛陽，安史之亂在兩京方向的戰局就此根本逆轉。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are concentrated in the Zizhi Tongjian, book 219, the thirty-fifth annal of the Tang. The date is the second month of the second year of Zhide (757), coming after the first month in which An Qingxu had killed his father An Lushan at Luoyang and taken the throne; the assault was launched on the night of the eleventh. On numbers of men, the Tongjian records that the Tang forces 'destroyed nearly a thousand of the rebels who held the city', and later, in the pursuit, 'destroyed four thousand of the enemy and captured five thousand'; the rebels who forced their way in at the gate of Anyi were wiped out, but their number is not given. On the Uyghur side the Tongjian records separately that Pugu Huai'en had borrowed seven thousand five hundred Uyghur riders on his own in the previous year; they marched with the army here, though they are not recorded as taking part in the assault on Hedong. As to distance, the straight line from Luojiao (present-day Fuxian, Shaanxi) to Puzhou in Hedong runs about two hundred and eighty li, a little over a hundred and forty kilometres, and the real march had to turn and twist along the channels of the Luo, the Wei and the Yellow River, taking a matter of days; from Puzhou to Anyi (northeast of present-day Yuncheng, Shanxi) is some sixty li, and from Anyi Cui Qianyou went on south over the White Path Ridge (northwest of present-day Pinglu, Shanxi) into Henan, a continuous flight completed inside a single day. The result carries a further figure with it: in the tenth month of the same year the Tang recovered Chang'an, and in the twelfth month they moved against Luoyang, and from that moment the course of the An Lushan rebellion in the region of the two capitals was turned outright.
cause: 起事有遠因近因兩層。遠因是自755年安史之亂以來，唐廷的西京、東京相繼淪陷，叛軍以河北為根基，關中則靠臨時徵發的市卒與降附之眾勉力支撐，兩京之間的交通線與糧道長期為叛軍所控，唐軍要反攻，非先在河東立足不可。近因是757年正月安慶緒在洛陽弒父安祿山、自立為帝，燕政權因繼承危機而內訧，肅宗乘機下詔收復兩京。郭子儀的判斷是：河東地處洛陽、長安之間，取之即可威攝潼關、切斷兩京聯繫；同時河東是燕軍河洛防線的支撐點，也是叛軍糧餉與河北消息往來的要道。策反之所以成功，也有客觀條件：安史集團並非鐵板一塊，崔乾祐麾下的唐朝舊軍與地方官吏在叛軍節制下久矣，一旦唐軍的旗號出現，內應這扇門就有人肯開。
causeEn: The campaign had a remote cause and a proximate one. The remote cause lies in the fact that since the An Lushan rebellion broke out in 755 the Western and Eastern Capitals of the Tang had fallen in turn; the rebels had their base in Hebei, while in Guanzhong they held together only by draftees hastily picked out of the towns of the capital and by the men who surrendered and joined them; the lines of communication and of supply between the two capitals stayed in rebel hands for a long time, and the Tang could not counter-attack without first establishing a footing in Hedong. The proximate cause was that in the first month of 757 An Qingxu killed his father An Lushan at Luoyang and took the throne, so that the Yan regime split over the succession, and the emperor took the chance to order the recovery of the two capitals. Guo Ziyi's reasoning was that Hedong lay between Luoyang and Chang'an, and that taking it would overawe Tong Pass and sever the link between the two capitals; at the same time Hedong was the hinge on which the Yan defensive line between the Yellow River and Luo rested, and the road along which the rebels' grain and their messages from Hebei travelled. The subversion of the garrison could succeed for reasons of its own: the An Lushan band was not a single block of iron, the old Tang soldiers and local officials under Cui Qianyou had long been under rebel command, and once the Tang banner appeared over the city there were men ready to open the door from inside.
impact: 河東歸唐的第一層影響在戰略位置。唐軍由此取得河中（蒲州）的城垣、倉廩與黃河渡口，一路由東可窺洛陽，一路向西經華州即可進逼長安，叛軍的河洛防線被從中間切開，潼關方向的壓力驟增。結果是同年十月唐軍收復西京長安，十二月進取東都洛陽，安慶緒北走，兩京光復，安史之亂由攻勢轉入守勢；河北的成德、范陽、平盧等軍鎮在失去中原之後各自孤立，叛軍的兵源與糧源被耗在河北一隅，唐軍則得以在河東就地補充兵員與糧秣。第二層影響在人事與制度。郭子儀以朔方節度使兼兵部尚書的資歷出師河東，其戰功與「不取河東則無以圖兩京」的判斷，進一步鞏固了他在唐廷軍務上的位置；僕固懷恩則因引回鶻兵、又統河東追擊之師而聲勢漸重，河中軍鎮自此在唐廷的藩鎮格局中正式成形。第三層在長遠：晚唐河中與河東兩大軍鎮彼此對峙，驕兵跋扈、爭奪河地，成為唐末藩鎮割據與中原混戰的重要源頭之一，這條線由757年的一場夜襲牽出。
impactEn: The first effect of Hedong's return to Tang hands was strategic and positional. The Tang army gained the walls, the granaries and the crossing on the Yellow River at Hezhong, the seat at Puzhou; from there one road looked east towards Luoyang and another ran west through Huazhou straight at Chang'an, so that the rebel line between the Yellow River and Luo was cut through the middle and the pressure on Tong Pass rose sharply. The result followed: in the tenth month of the same year the Tang recovered the Western Capital Chang'an, in the twelfth month they moved on the Eastern Capital Luoyang, An Qingxu fled north, the two capitals were restored, and the An Lushan rebellion turned from offensive to defensive. The circuit armies of Chengde, Fanyang and Pinglu in Hebei, cut off from the central plain, lay isolated and each after its own fashion, while the rebels' supply of men and grain was consumed in a corner of Hebei; the Tang, for their part, could replenish troops and provisions on the spot in Hedong. The second effect lay in men and in institutions. Guo Ziyi, who had marched out as Military Governor of Shuofang and Minister of War, added to a reputation already built on his judgement that without Hedong the two capitals could not be attempted, and his position in the military affairs of the court grew firmer; Pugu Huai'en gained weight through his part in bringing the Uyghurs and in commanding the pursuit out of Hedong, and the Hezhong garrison took its place in the Tang state as a military governorship in its own right. The third effect was a long one. In the late Tang the two great commands of Hezhong and Hedong stood across the river from one another, the soldiers of each growing insolent and the ground by the river fought over, and that quarrel became one of the principal sources of the military governors' separatism and of the wars that tore the central plain in the late ninth century, and the thread of it was drawn out of a night assault in 757.
result: 結果是唐軍攻克河東郡（蒲州），燕軍守將崔乾祐部覆沒。資治通鑑記城內守軍近千人被殲，郭旰與僕固懷恩在城北擊潰叛軍反攻，乘勝追擊又殲四千人、俘五千人；崔乾祐退至安邑城下，叛軍飢疲爭門，門閘驟落，預伏者截殺入城之眾，崔乾祐遂取道白徑嶺向河南方向逃去，唐軍順利占領河東。此役在戰術上最值得記取的一點，是攻方沒有在城牆下消耗兵力：策反在先、夜襲在後、追擊不停，三步銜接，於是守城一方賴以壓制進攻者的弩始終未能發揮作用，攻城器械、門樓與城頭火力全部落空。反過來，進攻方在野戰階段把弩陣與騎兵配合起來，使潰兵無路可走，遂把一場城池攻防變成城外的追殺。對全局而言，河東之戰是安史之亂的一個轉折點：兩京之間的樞紐回到唐軍之手，其後同年收復長安、洛陽，而至763年叛亂平定。崔乾祐此後的下落史書記載有限，僅知其南走白徑嶺、投向河南方向，其後所終不得詳。
resultEn: The outcome was that the Tang army captured Hedong Commandery at Puzhou and the force of the Yan garrison commander Cui Qianyou was destroyed. The Tongjian records that nearly a thousand of the defenders in the city were killed, that Guo Gan and Pugu Huai'en broke the rebel counter-attack north of the walls, and that the pursuit destroyed four thousand of the enemy and took five thousand prisoners. Driven back to the walls of Anyi, the hungry and exhausted rebels forced their way in at the gate, the gate was dropped behind them, the men posted in ambush cut down those who had got in, and Cui Qianyou took the road over the White Path Ridge towards Henan; the Tang then took Hedong without further trouble. The point of this campaign worth keeping in the mind is that the attackers spent no strength under the walls: the subversion came first, the night assault second, the pursuit never stopped, and the three were linked, so that the crossbow on which the defenders relied to hold the attackers off never once got the chance to fire, and the siege gear, the gate towers and the wall-top fire all fell flat. In the other direction, on the field after the capture, the attacking side combined the crossbow line with the horse so that the routed had nowhere to run, and a battle over a walled city was turned into a slaughter in the open outside it. In the wider war the battle of Hedong was a turning point of the An Lushan rebellion: the hinge between the two capitals came back into Tang hands, the two capitals were recovered later in the same year, and by 763 the rebellion was settled. What the histories do not carry on Cui Qianyou after this is thin; the last certain thing is that he went south over the White Path Ridge in the direction of Henan, and where he ended is not known.
